programme: NCOR1 and HDAC3 form the core of the NCoR1–SMRT/HDAC3 nuclear corepressor complex: NCOR1 scaffolds nuclear receptors (its target list includes its own paralog NCOR2, and receptor/coactivator genes RARB, ESR1, AR, NCOA3) and docks HDAC3, whose deacetylase activity is allosterically dependent on NCoR1's DAD domain; together they set the repressive baseline on growth, inflammatory and receptor-response genes (HDAC3 targets MYC, EGFR, VEGFA, TNF, TLR9, CDH1, MMP2).
role_in_a: In vascular/myeloid biology, the NCoR1–HDAC3 corepressor sets the threshold for NF-kB- and lipid-sensing nuclear-receptor-driven gene induction in macrophages and endothelium; when this repressive checkpoint is lost or altered, inflammatory and growth-factor genes (of the same class HDAC3 targets here: TNF, VEGFA) are derepressed, a mechanism implicated in vascular inflammation and plaque biology in the broader literature, though not the retrieved record for this pair.
role_in_b: In lung cancer the same complex is directly evidenced: HDAC3 is recruited to repress or de-repress tumor-relevant loci (SATB2–HDAC3–LCN2 axis, PMID 41736683), is a CRISPR-validated dependency and radiosensitizing target in small cell lung cancer (PMID 40899441), tracks with immunotherapy outcome (PMID 40506719) and is reviewed across pulmonary disease broadly (PMID 40097842); NCOR1 partners with RARα to control autophagy pathways exploited therapeutically in cancer (PMID 40490560).
shared_axis: Both atherosclerotic/vascular disease and lung cancer involve chronic tissue stress (vascular injury/lipid loading in one, hypoxic/proliferative tumor microenvironment in the other) in which the same NCoR1–HDAC3 repressive checkpoint gates NF-kB- and receptor-driven target genes (TNF, VEGFA, MYC, EGFR); the same complex could set inflammatory tone in vascular myeloid cells and growth/immune-evasion tone in lung tumor cells, without the two diseases needing a shared causal event.
reasoning: NCOR1–HDAC3 is a real, nameable corepressor complex and the lung-cancer leg is independently placed by four HDAC3 papers and one NCOR1 paper in the retrieved record; the cardiovascular leg, however, rests entirely on general corepressor/inflammation biology outside this record — Open Targets shows no association and no paper here places either factor in Cardiovascular_Disease, so the cross-disease connection is reasoned, not retrieved.
support: PMID 41736683 — SATB2 recruits HDAC3 to repress LCN2 and restrain lung tumor growth, showing HDAC3 acting as a locus-specific corepressor in lung cancer; PMID 40899441 — CRISPR screen shows HDAC3 is a radiosensitizing dependency in small cell lung cancer; PMID 40506719 — HDAC3 tracks with immunotherapy response and prognosis in advanced lung cancer; PMID 40097842 — review of HDAC3 across pulmonary disease generally; PMID 40490560 — small-molecule disruption of the RARα–NCoR1 interaction blocks chaperone-mediated autophagy in cancer, evidencing NCoR1-complex function as a druggable node. No PMID in the material places either factor in cardiovascular disease.
how_to_falsify: Treat vascular macrophages/endothelial cells under an atherogenic/inflammatory stimulus and an NSCLC or SCLC line under matched hypoxic/proliferative stress with a selective HDAC3 inhibitor (e.g. RGFP966) or NCOR1 knockdown, and measure the shared target set (VEGFA, TNF/NF-kB-responsive genes, MYC). If the shared corepressor checkpoint is real, both cell types should derepress these overlapping targets comparably; if only the lung tumor cells respond and the vascular cells show no change (or vice versa), the shared-axis claim fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood vs lung across 224 patient-group comparisons but only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the comparisons are not fully independent replicates. Both HDAC3 and NCOR1 are mid-ranked by recurrence (96/224, 43%), well below the top factors TEAD4 (119/224) and ELK4 (116/224), which were left out of this account because they do not mechanistically join the NCoR1–HDAC3 complex. The tissue-generic exclusion list is dominated by immune/lymphoid TFs (BCL3, BCL6, RELB, GFI1B, ID2, ID3, NFATC1), so HDAC3/NCOR1 surviving is not simply a 'blood is immune tissue' artifact — but the complete absence of any Open Targets or literature hit for Cardiovascular_Disease across every factor in this list is a real gap, not filled by this account, and the single-view list (FOXI1, SALL2, etc.) confirms this story is not built on one outlier subgroup.
